title: The Evergreen Game
line: Anderssen against Dufresne, Berlin 1852: an attack down the open lines.

steps.text: Berlin, 1852. Anderssen gave a pawn early for open lines. Black's king is still in the middle, facing his rook and bishops.
Anderssen gave his knight to bring a pawn to f6. White was winning before this move; after it, best defense would make the game level.
Bring your last rook to the file next to Black's king, behind your bishop. Engines rate this level: Black had a defense.
steps.after: Black takes your knight and threatens mate next to your king.

steps.text: Take the knight on e7 with check.
steps.after: The other knight takes back, and Black's king loses its shield.

steps.text: Give your queen with check on d7. If the king steps aside instead of taking, it is mated at once.
steps.after: The king takes, right in front of your rook and bishop.

steps.text: Move the bishop with check. Your rook behind it checks too: a double check.
steps.after: Only a king move answers a double check.
Checkmate. The pawn on f6 and the bishop on d7 guard the rest.

summary: Anderssen opened files toward a king left in the middle, then gave his queen to drive it into a double check.
